instructions: Present the plan day by day in a practical order.
Distinguish confirmed details from estimates and local-confirmation items.

criteria.description: Every element of the plan must be achievable with the stated transport situation. Recommending an unsealed-road destination to a standard hire car, or an unreachable site to a visitor without a vehicle, is a violation unless clearly flagged with an alternative.
criteria.title: The plan is feasible with the stated transport

criteria.description: The plan should address distances, fuel or supply points, safety precautions, connectivity, and booking lead times where relevant, not just list attractions.
criteria.title: Remote-area practicalities are addressed

criteria.description: Road access, opening, and tour availability claims for remote areas change often and must be supported by suitably fresh sources.
criteria.title: Access and condition claims are supported by current sources

criteria.description: Where reliable current information is unavailable, the answer should say so and advise how to confirm locally, rather than presenting guesses as facts.
criteria.title: Sparse or conflicting information is acknowledged

transport.description: a two-wheel-drive campervan they also sleep in

traveller.description: two adults, one of whom uses a wheelchair

prompt:
Two adults, one of whom uses a wheelchair is planning 4 days
based in Broome, WA, travelling
with a two-wheel-drive campervan they also sleep in.

Outline a realistic plan for the visit. Treat the practicalities of a remote
area as first-class concerns: driving distances and road surfaces, fuel and
supply points, water and heat precautions, mobile coverage, seasonal or
weather-dependent road access, and how far ahead accommodation, fuel stops,
or tours must be booked. Recommend experiences that genuinely suit the
transport situation, and say clearly what is not feasible with it. Where
current information is thin or conflicting for this area, say so explicitly
rather than guessing, and cite the sources you relied on close to the
relevant statements.
